episode_title: The End of Free Money in the Condo Market

real_qa.q: Why have pre-construction condo sales in Vancouver declined by more than half since 2021?
real_qa.r: Pre-construction sales are down more than half from 2021 levels in Vancouver. Investors who previously dominated this market—representing about 70% of pre-construction sales—have fled due to eroding cash flows from higher mortgage rates that no longer cover carrying costs, combined with falling resale prices. Developers have stopped launching marketing campaigns because banks require approximately 60% of units to be pre-sold before providing financing, making it too risky when demand has collapsed.

real_qa.q: What percentage of development fees and costs account for new housing prices in Vancouver and Toronto?
real_qa.r: Government fees and taxes account for close to 30% of the cost of new housing in Vancouver and Toronto. These include 5% GST, 2% property transfer tax in BC, and approximately 3% in realtor fees, totaling around 10% in immediate fees and taxes that purchasers must hurdle over, plus the city development charges component.
real_qa.requete: development fees percentage cost housing Vancouver Toronto

real_qa.q: How much have rents declined in Vancouver and Toronto over the past 18 months?
real_qa.r: Rents in Vancouver and Toronto are down about 10% over the past approximately 18 months. This rental decline, combined with falling resale prices and rising mortgage rates, creates a squeeze for condo investors who are renewing mortgages at 4% instead of the previous 2% rates.
real_qa.requete: rent decline Vancouver Toronto 18 months percentage

real_qa.q: What is the GTA at in terms of new home sales compared to historical lows?
real_qa.r: The GTA has reached a 30-year low in new home sales. Vancouver is at approximately a six or seven-year low, with pre-construction sales in 2024 down more than half compared to 2021 levels.

real_qa.q: Why are Canadian banks offering blanket appraisals at original purchase prices for troubled condo units?
real_qa.r: Banks are offering blanket appraisals at original purchase prices—sometimes resulting in loan-to-value ratios of 90-100% or more—because those same banks often hold the construction loan for the developer. By enabling buyers to close through favorable appraisals, banks avoid forcing the developer into default while kicking the can down the road, hoping the market will recover within two to seven years before addressing potential losses.
real_qa.requete: blanket appraisals condo units Canadian banks why

real_qa.q: What types of housing products are developers building today instead of high-rise condos?
real_qa.r: Developers are now building low-rise wood frame buildings—typically five to six-story structures in the purpose-built rental space—and ground-oriented duplex and triplex-style housing. High-rise condos are not being built because they are expensive, require speculative investors, and there is no pre-construction market for them. Wood frame buildings are cost-effective and quick to build, while ground-oriented housing appeals to young families seeking more space and backyards.
